newsitem.title: USA: Thoratec sees Q1 shr loss $0.07-$0.08.
newsitem.headline: Thoratec sees Q1 shr loss $0.07-$0.08.

text.p: Thoratec Laboratories Corp said it expected a first quarter earnings loss of between $0.07 and $0.08 per share on revenues of about $2 million due to lower patient demand and slower sales to a distributor.

The company said it saw low overall patient demand in January and part of February and a slowdown in sales to its main European distributor as the company prepared to sell directly to much of Europe in the second half of 1997.
The First Call mean earnings estimate for the quarter was a loss of $0.04 per share compared to a loss of $0.08 per share in the year-ago first quarter.

The company, which researches, develops, makes and markets medical devices for circulatory support and vascular graft appplications, said it continued to invest in product research and development and its marketing capabilities.

"While we enjoyed record domestic sales in the month of March, we experienced an apparent segment-wide slowdown in the early portion of the quarter, that represents the month- to-month variability occasionally seen in the cardiac transplant arena," D. Keith Grossman, Thoratec's president and chief executive officer, said.
Thoratec said its decision to sell directly in Germany, France and Spain starting in July would hurt its international sales in the first half of the year.

"We are now in the process of establishing our direct presence in these markets," Grossman said. "This change, along with the planned new product introductions and regulatory filings on track for this year, should position us well for the second half of 1997 and beyond."
